title: Verification receipt
description: A compact, replayable record of what was checked and what the result was. Emitted per protocol pack and once for the whole repository. A receipt supports inspection and replay; it is not independent trust, correctness or impact evidence. Timestamps are commit-derived, never clock-derived, so the same committed source yields the same receipt.

scope.description: Whether this receipt covers one pack or the whole candidate.

subject_id.description: Protocol id, or 'productivity-protocols' for a repository receipt.

source_commit.description: Short commit the receipt was generated from. Null outside a git checkout.

source_commit_full.description: Full Git commit identity. Null outside a Git checkout.

source_tree.description: Git tree object for the committed source. A release is valid only when dirty is false.

source_date.description: Commit date (ISO 8601). The build's only clock.

dirty.description: Whether tracked or untracked working-tree content differed from the named commit before verification. Null outside Git.

node.description: Reviewed Node compatibility range for reproducible receipt bytes. The exact replay runtime belongs in the CI or build log.

checks.description: Each verification gate that ran, in order.

files_sha256.description: Every file covered by this receipt, with its hash.

assurance_status.description: The assurance-ladder state the checks justify. Never exceeds what the checks actually establish.

productivity_evidence.description: The evidence-ladder state, carried from the protocol record. A structural receipt does not raise this.

command.description: The single command that reproduces this receipt from a clean checkout.

condition.description: The source-state condition under which replay is or is not promised.
